_label_audit: Every label declared below is classified (control/human-signal/vestigial) with writer/reader evidence in ../../docs/label-audit.md. Read it before adding, removing, or repurposing any label here.
_vocabulary_note: The `vocabulary` object below (tracker-event-vocabulary-and-emitter, Phase B1) is the board-agnostic event catalog lib/events.sh's emit_event validates against. It is a separate namespace from `triggers` on purpose — `triggers` is Linear-specific board-driver data (from/to state names, add/remove label names) that flow.sh executes unchanged; `vocabulary` describes what happened in pipeline terms, never a Linear column or label. A vocabulary entry's optional `trigger` field names the single state-machine trigger it is a 1:1 fact-equivalent of, consumed by flow.sh's generic post-mutation dual-write (Section 6 of that change); entries with no `trigger` field are emitted by a specific non-generic call site instead (see each event's `emitted_by`).

planned.description: Provenance marker — ticket was generated by ticket-planner. Once set, never removed by any pipeline phase.

INIT-*.description: Wildcard pattern matching initiative IDs (e.g., INIT-42). Links ticket to parent planning initiative. Never removed.

pre-approved.description: Set by planner when confidence >= 0.85. Accelerates ticket-appraise fast-path eligibility (skips full codebase investigation). Does NOT bypass the human approval gate — the standard gate rules (complex → human approved, simple+auto → auto-approve) still apply regardless of pre-approved.

blocked-by:*.description: Wildcard pattern for dependency enforcement (e.g., blocked-by:CRE-100). Auto-removed when the blocking ticket reaches Done.

state:execution.description: Marks an initiative Epic as ready for fleet controller dispatch. Epic-only. Applied directly by the planner (never through a flow.sh trigger), so the must_be_epic precondition that used to sit here had no trigger to attach to — removed by tracker-flow-projection-cutover rather than relocated; the enforcement question moves to the next change, which addresses the planner's own writes.

bug.description: Type label — task is a bug fix. Set by planner at ticket creation. Never removed.

feature.description: Type label — task is a new feature. Set by planner at ticket creation. Never removed.

improvement.description: Type label — task is an improvement to existing functionality. Set by planner at ticket creation. Never removed.

security.description: Type label — task is a security fix or hardening. Set by planner at ticket creation. Never removed.

chore.description: Type label — task is a maintenance chore (dependency updates, refactoring, tooling). Set by planner at ticket creation. Never removed.

appraise-start.description: Claim a ticket and begin appraisal

human-reject.description: Human rejected the plan — return to Todo for re-appraisal

implement-outcome.description: Record implementation difficulty (Smooth/Rough/Hard) locally — no longer a tracker label

pr-review-pass-done.description: PR approved with no UAT required — close to Done

pr-review-pass-uat.description: PR approved with UAT required — move to UAT

pr-review-fail.description: PR review found issues — mark rejected (no state change)

pr-iterate.description: Iterating on PR feedback — return to Ready

uat-fail.description: UAT failed — return to Ready for another pass

needs-info.description: Block ticket — waiting for external information

needs-adr.description: Block ticket — parked or stopped on an ADR gate CREATED_PROPOSED/SUPERSEDE_REQUIRED/CONFLICT verdict

needs-adr-resolved.description: Unblock ticket — the governing ADR has been accepted

re-claim.description: Remove approval label to restart gate hold cycle

epic-integration-open.description: Epic integration PRs are open — epic moves to Review.

epic-uat-start.description: Epic integration merged and deployed — epic moves to UAT.

epic-uat-pass.description: Epic UAT accepted — epic moves to Done. Deliberately no verdict_gate (issue #368): no phase ever writes a per-epic META|verifier-result against the epic issue's own log — verifier-results are written by child-ticket phases (VERIFY/PR-REVIEW) against each child's own log. A verdict_gate here would read an always-empty per-epic verifier history and never block anything, which is worse than no gate at all — it would look load-bearing without being one.

appraise-started.description: A ticket was claimed and appraisal began.

human-rejected.description: A human rejected the plan — returned for re-appraisal.

implement-completed.description: Implementation was pushed — entering code review.

pr-review-passed.description: A PR review passed. Collapses the destination-encoding pr-review-pass-done/pr-review-pass-uat trigger pair into one fact carrying whether UAT is required next. Emitted by flow.sh itself (via each trigger's own emits declaration), after the verdict gate has allowed the transition — not by the branch-resolve.sh helper that resolves which destination applies, which would emit before the transition is attempted.

pr-review-failed.description: PR review found issues — marked rejected, no state change.

pr-iteration-requested.description: Iterating on PR feedback — returned to Ready.

uat-failed.description: UAT failed — returned to Ready for another pass.

needs-info-requested.description: Ticket blocked — waiting for external information.

needs-adr-requested.description: Ticket blocked — parked on an ADR gate CREATED_PROPOSED/SUPERSEDE_REQUIRED/CONFLICT verdict.

needs-adr-resolved.description: Ticket unblocked — the governing ADR was accepted.

re-claimed.description: Approval label removed to restart the gate-hold cycle.

epic-integration-opened.description: Epic integration PRs are open — epic moved to Review.

epic-uat-started.description: Epic integration merged and deployed — epic moved to UAT.

epic-uat-passed.description: Epic UAT accepted — epic moved to Done.

gate-held.description: A ticket was held at the entry or re-approval gate. Does not call flow.sh — a hold changes no Linear label or state.

gate-released.description: A held gate was released and the ticket proceeded. provenance distinguishes human release from automatic re-evaluation.

human-hold-requested.description: An agent asked a human a question it could not proceed without. Does not call flow.sh.

human-hold-released.description: A human-hold request was answered and the pipeline resumed.

pr-opened.description: A pull request was created for the ticket.

pr-merged.description: The ticket's PR merged. Source of truth is runs.jsonl's merge entry; emitted only after META|outcome is already written — never from inside the phase-completion path that writes it.

verify-failed-retrying.description: A VERIFY attempt failed and the router is retrying, up to the loop cap.

blocked.description: The ticket entered the Blocked state, waiting on one or more blockers. No workflow.json trigger names Blocked as a from/to state — this fact exists in the vocabulary independent of any trigger.

unblocked.description: The ticket left the Blocked state — its blockers resolved.

_board_drivers_note: Per-board driver tables mapping this file's `vocabulary` events to a specific board's columns/labels (tracker-flow-projection-cutover, Change 2 of the tracker-decoupling authority-flip programme). `board_drivers.<board_id>` is the ONE sanctioned place in this file where a board-specific column or label name may appear — see the `pipeline-event-vocabulary` and `tracker-board-driver-contract` capabilities for the namespace rule this implements. Every vocabulary event has an entry below, an object or an explicit `null` (`null` means the event deliberately projects nothing — never means 'forgotten'; the coverage test in test-workflow-vocabulary.sh fails on a genuinely missing entry). `projected_labels` is the complete set of labels the linear driver may add or remove; every other label on an issue (a hand-applied `bug`, `security`, or a still-planner-written label like `planned`) is preserved untouched. Where an event is produced by exactly one trigger, that entry's add/remove SHALL equal the trigger's own adds/removes intersected with `projected_labels` — kept honest by the same coverage test, since this table intentionally duplicates the trigger's label delta rather than back-referencing it (design.md Decision 1: a third of the vocabulary has no trigger at all, and a second board needs its own projection of the same event).
